comparator.name: Educational Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The full-time Dutch-taught bachelor has 60 EC each year. Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 2 carries 6 EC; mandatory Academic Skills A and B carry zero credits. Year three includes 30 EC of electives or minor study and an 18 EC empirical thesis.

components.name: Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 1
Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 2
components.note: Academic Skills A and B are also mandatory in year one. They carry zero credits. Students must also attend nine scientific colloquium presentations during the bachelor.

components.name: Testing and Measurement
components.note: Attend Descriptive Statistics before Testing and Measurement. Research methods and statistics provide its foundation.

components.name: Lifelong Learning: Personal, Organisational and Societal Perspectives
The Future of Learning and Technology
Inferential Statistics
components.note: Pass Descriptive Statistics before Inferential Statistics.

components.name: Research Practice in Educational Sciences
components.note: Pass Descriptive Statistics and Testing and Measurement before this research-practice course.

components.name: Learning and Innovating in Organisations
components.note: Educational Sciences students must pass Organisation of Learning and Education before this consultancy project with external organisations.

components.name: Empirical Bachelor’s Thesis in Educational Sciences
components.note: Complete all first- and second-year requirements before starting, with an exception for one of six specified second-year subject courses. The thesis involves empirical research and individual written and oral reporting.

components.name: Free-Choice Electives or Minor
components.note: Choose related electives or a minor for 30 EC. First-year electives require permission unless they form part of a completed minor. Language-skills courses are excluded, and courses outside the faculty require Examination Board approval.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three options address learning and development through social and educational research, cognition and learning technology, or workplace development and organisational change. Each maintains a different substantive emphasis.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce empirical research design, measurement and analysis.
Both teach qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation. UvA focuses on educational questions.
Both develop statistical skills for social or behavioural research. UCR also applies multivariable models.
Both consider development and learning. UCR studies development across life, while UvA introduces pedagogical and educational science.
Both use ethical reasoning and argument. UvA focuses specifically on educational ideals and rights.
Both study policy decisions and processes. UCR uses a general policy case, while UvA studies the education system.
Both examine inequality and social institutions. UCR includes education among its social contexts, while UvA studies educational systems in depth.
Both use economic reasoning to study public investment and social outcomes. UCR includes education spending among its applications.
Both develop empirical research through practical work. UCR uses surveys about leadership and social experience, while UvA studies education.
Both study organisations, people and change. UvA applies organisational theory to learning and education.
